reason: Both are global alternatives-oriented asset managers that earn fees on assets managed and serve institutions plus individual or wealth clients. Cohen & Steers focuses on actively managed listed real assets and alternative income (REITs, listed infrastructure, commodities, preferreds) sold through funds and ETFs. GCM Grosvenor focuses on private-markets and multi-manager alternatives (private equity co-investments, hedge fund portfolios, infrastructure) built as customized programs. The investor base and fee model overlap, but the core products differ, so this is adjacent rather than direct.
